name: Mustard
grown_as: White mustard, sown as a quick green manure (as in William's records) and for 'mustard and cress' seedlings. ⚠️ CHECK: William's records also list 'Red Frills' as a salad leaf under Sinapis alba, but Red Frills is Brassica juncea, a different plant with deeply cut, frilly, red-purple leaves. Drawn as white mustard.
habit: An upright, branched annual 30 to 80 cm (to 1 m or more as a green manure), fast-growing, the stems with stiff, downward-pointing bristles.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, all on stalks; a loose rosette when young
leaf.type: Simple but deeply lobed (pinnately lobed, like a lyre): a large end lobe and two to four pairs of smaller side lobes
leaf.outline: Oval to oblong, 5 to 15 cm long, the end lobe broad and rounded and much the biggest
leaf.base: Narrowing into the stalk, the lowest lobes small
leaf.margin: Coarsely and irregularly toothed all round, on every lobe
leaf.veins: A pale midrib and side veins running into the lobes
leaf.surface: Rough with scattered stiff bristly hairs on both sides

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, oval with a short claw, spreading flat
flower.behind: Four narrow green sepals spreading out flat between the petals
flower.carried: In spikes at the tops of the stems and branches, opening from the bottom up
flower.season: June to August (about six weeks after sowing)

fruit: Pods 2 to 4 cm spreading out from the stem, bristly-hairy, swollen over two to four seeds on each side, ending in a long, flat, sword-shaped beak as long as or longer than the seed-bearing part. Seeds round, 2 to 2.5 mm, pale yellow.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, large for the seed; the first true leaves hairy and lobed.
winter: Nothing: an annual, killed by hard frost; as a green manure it is cut down or dug in before winter.

leaf: a lyre-shaped lobed leaf with a large rounded end lobe
bloom: four bright yellow petals in a cross
narrow sepals spreading out flat between them
seed: smooth, about the size of a pinhead
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
the first true leaf hairy and lobed
young: a small upright plant of lobed, toothed, bristly leaves
leaves on stalks up a short stem
crop: leafy upright plants of lobed, toothed leaves
flower: an upright branched plant with bright yellow flowers in spikes at the tops
seedhead: bristly pods spreading out from the stem
each with a long flat beak as long as the rest of the pod

look_alikes: Charlock (Sinapis arvensis) has less lobed upper leaves and pods with a shorter beak. Oilseed rape and turnip have smooth blue-green clasping stem leaves. Rocket has cream, purple-veined flowers. Brassica juncea mustards have smooth or frilly leaves and slender pods with a short beak.
